Can we triage and surface immediate mitigations (both customer-facing knobs and internal routing changes)? Priorities: restore interactive experience for their demo, then full RCA.

Suggested immediate mitigations to consider while infra investigates:
- Temporary: switch their calls to non-streaming responses (streaming=false) — this will increase perceived time-to-first-token, but avoids chunk hang-ups in some cases.
- Reduce max_tokens and response_chunk_size in the client to reduce token burst spikes.
- Enable prefix caching for frequent prompts (if applicable) to avoid repeated decoder compute.
- Route Lumina traffic to the dedicated smaller-llm variant (rwd-small-v2) as a fallback if larger model shows congestion.
- If routing change needed, do a canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor 95/99p latency.

Vivek, can you surface whether there are kernel-level queuing bursts on the US-west pools right now? Laura, please prepare a short customer note with recommended client-side knobs. I can send the outgoing message once we've agreed on wording.

Hi Ben — thanks for the data and the latency dump. We’re actively triaging on our side; summary and immediate mitigations below.

What we know so far:
- Root cause (investigation ongoing): intermittent queuing on our US-west inference pool affecting streaming chunk dispatch. This is causing delayed chunk availability for some sessions and creating the 3–8s hangs you saw.
- Scope: roughly 25–35% of streaming requests from your workspace during the window you reported. Non-streaming endpoints (batch/text-generation) appear unaffected.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations to apply right now:
1) Client-side quick fix (recommended for your demo): set streaming=false in the API call. This will cause the model to return a single complete response instead of many streamed chunks and avoids the chunk-hang behavior. Example: POST /v1/chat?streaming=false
2) Reduce per-response token budget: set max_tokens to 256 and reduce response_chunk_size to 64. This lowers per-chunk compute and reduces burst queuing.
3) Fallback routing (we can apply): we can route your workspace to rwd-small-v2 as a temporary fallback. It has slightly different token behavior but stable streaming characteristics under current load. We recommend a phased canary: 10% for 10m -> 50% for 15m -> 100% and we’ll watch 95/99p latency.

Actions we are taking (internal):
- Engineering already deployed a targeted routing change for affected US-west hosts to reduce queuing pressure.
- We enabled additional short-lived capacity in that pool and tightened the scheduler’s fairness window for high-concurrency sessions.
- We captured diagnostics and the attached routing-change-summary.pdf and monitoring snapshot for your review.

Next steps and timeline:
- Immediate: please try switching streaming=false for your demo and/or request the fallback routing. I can enact the routing change now if you authorize it.
- Short-term (within 6–12 hours): we expect queuing to be stable following the routing change; we will update you when 95/99p latency is back to normal.
- Full RCA & postmortem: we’ll provide a written RCA by EOD Oct 13 with root cause and permanent mitigations.

If you want, I can be on standby for the demo and coordinate the routing canary live.

Sorry for the disruption — we know this is high impact and we're treating it as an incident.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference
